                                          W2                                                        W5Why do we backpropagate?


     •  Let’s think about the problem of w-modification, and let’s
     compare the last set of w’s and the first
     •  Last W5: The output probabilities are directly determined by
      the Last w’s!!!! The error is very directly determined by the last
      W’s
     • We can use the error between computed and desired directly
      to determine better w’s.
     •  First W2 affects its activations, which affects another 2 layers
      of activations along with other W’s. It’s really hard to figure out
      the culpability of W2 for the mistakes made all the way at the
       end!!!!! Moreover, the effect of W2 on errors INCLUDES the
       effect of W5 on them, since W5 is downstream of W2!!!!
     • So which problem is easier: Improving W2 or W5?
     • W5 is easy! What algorithm do we use to solve small problems
     then bigger ones that depend on them?
     • Dynamic programming?
     •  Backpropagation is Bellman-Viterbi Dynamic Programming!!!
     •  Backpropagation = SGD + Dynamic programming 😉

The sigmoid activation function


                                                     σ(z) = 1 / (1 + exp(−z))        Lord Edgar Adrian

    Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, 1932

  Neurons are nearly digital! On or off, roughly.
           If the inner product is large positive,
 sigmoid function is near 1, and if inner product
      Is large negative, sigmois is basically 0.
Animal perception reflects this: some things that seem
alike, are perceived different, and some things that are
         Very different are perceived same!

                     If the inner product is −4:
           σ(−4) = 0.0180

                      If the inner product is 4:
            σ(4) = 0.9820
